task.description: RE-GATE after design revision. This is the same design doc you FAILED at BLOCKER severity in your prior pass (step-02b-code-design-validator.json) -- read your own prior finding in full again, then read the revised lib/letflow/design/iss0400-nested-parallel-gateway-fix.md fresh, focusing on section 2.3 (resolve_nested_split/3's mechanism, now claimed to share rather than reset Tarjan stack state), section 3.2 (a new worked trace claimed to walk through your own exact counterexample graph step by step), and section 3.3 (claimed to no longer contradict 2.3). Do not accept CODE-DESIGNER's claim that the revised trace is correct -- independently re-derive it yourself against your own counterexample graph (outer_split -> A -> inner_split, branch ia -> A back-edge, branch ib -> inner_join -> post -> outer_join, exactly as you specified it in your prior FAIL), tracing the REVISED algorithm (no reset at the resolve_nested_split/3 boundary, full state sharing) step by step to confirm it actually terminates and actually detects the back-edge to A correctly this time. Also check whether the new state-sharing mechanism reopens either of the two defect classes ISS-0398's own design already fixed once (naive-visited-set-copy DoS blowup; memo-key unsoundness under legal cycles) via some new angle the removal of the reset might introduce -- sharing more state is not automatically safe merely because resetting less state was the fix. Also verify the design doc's own §2.3/§3.3 contradiction is genuinely gone, not merely reworded to appear reconciled. Re-check the design's new fixture 3 (nested_split_ancestor_back_edge_graph/0) and its stated negative twin (fixture 3b) actually match the graph shape they claim to test. Every other acceptance criterion from the original gate (memo-key soundness for the non-cyclic case, @max_nodes arithmetic, zero-split-role-fixtures claim, :dead_end propagation, no .ex bodies) was already verified sound in your prior pass and does not need re-verification unless this revision touched those sections -- check whether it did (per CODE-DESIGNER's own summary, sections 3.4/6/7 were also updated to match) and re-verify only what changed.
acceptance_criteria: The revised resolve_nested_split/3 mechanism (state-sharing, no reset) is independently re-traced against your own exact counterexample graph from the prior FAIL, confirming genuine termination and correct back-edge detection -- not accepted from CODE-DESIGNER's own trace

The revised mechanism is checked against both defect classes ISS-0398's own design already fixed (naive-visited-set DoS, memo-key unsoundness) for whether increased state-sharing reopens either from a new angle
The prior section 2.3/3.3 internal contradiction is confirmed genuinely resolved, not just reworded
Sections 3.4/6/7 (or any other section CODE-DESIGNER's own summary says it touched) are re-checked for consistency with the revised mechanism
New fixtures 3 and 3b are checked against the graph shapes they claim to represent
No .ex implementation bodies present in the design doc
Verdict is PASS or FAIL with every issue at BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR severity named specifically

result.summary:
PASS -- the BLOCKER from step-02b (iteration 1's reset-at-the-resolve_nested_split/3-boundary defect) is genuinely fixed, not merely reworded. Independently re-derived, node by node, the revised (no-reset, full-state-sharing) algorithm against my own exact counterexample graph from the prior FAIL (outer_split -> A -> inner_split (:split, out-degree 2); edge a: inner_split -> ia -> A (back-edge); edge b: inner_split -> ib -> inner_join -> post -> outer_join), without accepting the design doc's own §3.2 trace as given:

My independent trace: branch 0 resolves outer_join via the unchanged step-4 :join/:pass_through arm (PARALLEL_GATEWAY never pushed to stack), memo[outer_join] written, stack empties. Branch 1 begins with find_matching_join/2's own top-level reset (the only reset anywhere in this revision) -- index/lowlink/stack/stack_set/next_index cleared, memo carried forward. A: fresh, index=0, pushed, stack=[A], stack_set={A}. A's edge -> inner_split: fresh, index=1, pushed, stack=[inner_split,A], stack_set={A,inner_split}. gateway_role(inner_split)=:split -> resolve_nested_split(inner_split, state) fires with stack_set still containing A (no reset performed at this boundary, confirmed against the literal text of revised §2.3/§2.3's own fold description). Inside the fold, continuing the SAME index/stack sequence: edge a -> ia: fresh, index=2, pushed, stack=[ia,inner_split,A]; ia's edge -> A: step-1 memo miss, step-2 on-stack check -- A IS in stack_set (never wiped) -- returns {:open, index[A]=0}, MapSet.new() for this branch, a genuine correctly-detected live back-edge, with NO re-exploration of A and NO second call into inner_split. Back in ia: local_lowlink=min(2,0)=0, closure check 0!=2 fails, ia stays on stack, returns {:open,0}. Edge b -> ib: fresh, index=3, pushed; ib's edge -> inner_join: :join role, immediate terminal (no stack push), leaves={gateway,inner_join}, memoized; ib closes trivially (3==3), pops. Back in resolve_nested_split's fold over inner_split: branch a gave {:open,0}, branch b gave {:finished,{gateway,inner_join}} -- per §2.3's agreement rule this counts as agreement (the open branch contributes no leaf and only pulls lowlink down). inner_split's own local_leaves={gateway,inner_join}, local_lowlink=min(1,0)=0. Continuation step resolves inner_join's outgoing edge into post (fresh, index=4, pushed) -> outer_join (step-1 memo hit from branch 0) -> {:finished,{gateway,outer_join}}; post closes trivially, pops. inner_split's own closure check uses ITS OWN local_lowlink (0, not the continuation call's tag) -- 0 != index[inner_split]=1 -- so inner_split returns {:open,0},{gateway,outer_join} and stays on stack (not popped, no memo entry). Back in A's frame: child tag {:open,0} -> A's local_leaves={gateway,outer_join}, local_lowlink=min(0,0)=0==index[A]=0 -> A is the SCC root, pops stack=[ia,inner_split,A] down through A (all three members), writes memo[ia]=memo[inner_split]=memo[A]={gateway,outer_join}. Branch 1's top-level result is {gateway,outer_join}, matching branch 0's singleton -- find_matching_join/2 returns {:ok,outer_join}. Every node (A, inner_split, ia, ib, inner_join, post, outer_join) is visited exactly once as a fresh exploration; resolve_nested_split/3 is entered exactly once, never re-entered; the back-edge ia->A is correctly detected via the ordinary step-2 on-stack check because stack_set was never reset. This independently confirms genuine termination and correct back-edge/SCC-closure detection -- my trace matches the design doc's own §3.2 trace node-for-node and index-for-index, so it is confirmed sound rather than merely plausible-looking.

Defect-class re-hunt (not accepted from the design's own §3.1/§3.2 argument, re-derived from a fresh angle): (1) DoS/exponential-blowup class (ISS-0398's iteration-1-to-2 fix) -- that defect required a per-path COPY of visited/state; this revision's resolve_nested_split/3 threads the identical state value (never copies), so the step-1 memo-hit short-circuit still applies uniformly across nesting boundaries (confirmed directly in my own trace: ib's target inner_join is memoized once, any second path to it would get an O(1) hit) -- no new per-path recomputation is introduced by sharing MORE state (memo already was shared in iteration 1; only stack/index/lowlink additionally stopped being reset -- reset vs. share was never the dimension the copy-vs-memo blowup defect turned on, so removing the reset does not reopen that class). (2) Memo-key-unsoundness class (ISS-0398's iteration-2-to-3 fix, order-dependent memo values from different entry points into one cycle) -- checked from a fresh angle: could a node reachable from two different outer-branch calls (memo persists across top-level branches, stack/index resets per top-level branch) get two different memo values now that resolve_nested_split/3 shares stack too? No new mechanism is introduced: nesting is not a second traversal context, it is the same continuous pass: resolve_nested_split/3 never writes memo[gw_node.id] itself (confirmed at design lines 340-374, unchanged claim, independently re-checked against the revised no-reset mechanism specifically -- the removal of the reset does not change which calls write memo, only whether stack_set visibility crosses the resolve_nested_split/3 boundary) -- every memo write still happens at an ordinary step-5 SCC closure, the same closure rule ISS-0398 already proved order-independent. No new angle found that reopens either defect class.

§2.3/§3.3 contradiction check: grepped every occurrence of 'reset' in the revised document (36 hits). Every occurrence is one of: (a) describing the rejected iteration-1 mechanism explicitly labeled as rejected, (b) the single unchanged find_matching_join/2 top-level per-branch reset, or (c) an explicit statement that no reset happens at the resolve_nested_split/3 boundary. The :open-propagation rule is stated identically in §2.3 (lines 260-270) and §3.3 (lines 654-671) -- word-for-word the same rule, not two different accounts reconciled by rewording. Genuinely resolved.

Fixture re-check against claimed graph shapes: fixture 3 (nested_split_ancestor_back_edge_graph/0, design lines 770-804) matches my own independently-traced counterexample graph exactly and its assertions (succeeds, resolves to outer_join, terminates in bounded time, join_counters keyed on the real outer join) all follow from my independent trace above. Fixture 3b (lines 806-817, second back-edge inner_split->ib->A replacing the escape edge): independently traced -- A(idx0)->inner_split(idx1)->resolve_nested_split, no reset; edge a ia(idx2)->A on-stack->{:open,0},empty; edge b ib(idx3)->A on-stack->{:open,0},empty; both branches open with no finished leaf, inner_split's local_leaves stays empty, local_lowlink=min(1,0,0)=0; back in A: local_leaves=empty, local_lowlink=0==index[A]=0, A closes as SCC root {A,inner_split,ia,ib} with an EMPTY aggregate leaf set -- correctly fails the non-singleton-agreement check (§2.5, unchanged) and propagates as {:error,{:no_matching_join_found,"outer_split"}}, matching the fixture's stated assertion, and terminates (no hang) via the same SCC-closure mechanism. Both fixtures match their claimed shapes and assertions.

Sections re-checked for consistency with the revised mechanism per the handoff's instruction (3.4/6/7, per CODE-DESIGNER's own summary): §3.4's termination argument for arbitrary nesting depth correctly extends the unchanged ISS-0398 O(nodes+edges) bound without amendment, consistent with the no-reset mechanism (no new per-path work, verified above) -- checked graph.ex directly, @max_nodes 500 confirmed live at lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex:158, matching the design's citation; the >=3-nodes-per-nesting-level arithmetic and the resulting depth bound of 166 is arithmetically correct. §6 (signature/name summary) correctly and explicitly instructs ELIXIR-DEV never to call reset_stack_bookkeeping/1 inside resolve_nested_split/3 or its call chain, consistent with §2.3/§3.2's mechanism, and correctly restricts reset_stack_bookkeeping/1's only call site to find_matching_join/2's own top-level fold, unchanged. §7's open questions are implementation-judgment items only (helper extraction, :combined_unsupported diagnosability, unit-vs-end-to-end fixture testing) and introduce no new deferral of a required design element -- none of them leave an acceptance criterion unaddressed. No .ex implementation bodies present anywhere in the document (confirmed by direct full read of both halves of the file, lines 1-924 -- only @spec/@type fences and prose, matching ISS-0398's own convention).

No BLOCKER, MAJOR, or MINOR issues found in this re-gate. Routes to ELIXIR-DEV for Step 2a implementation.
